text: You have a strange, fleeting dream as you wake.  You are making a stand at a coastline encircled by otherworldly storm, firing upon a black leviathan amongst men you believe to be kin.  It's so vivid you can feel the roar of the cannons vibrating in your spine.
You are submerged in a sea of what looks like TV static.  It is thick to the point you cannot see your hands in front of your face, but you make out faint shapes in the distance.  Then you wake up.

You have a memory, or something that feels like one, of being swarmed shoulder to shoulder by the undead horde.  But you are not in danger.  With every flinch and movement you make, you turn dozens into a thick red-black paste.  There is hardly any effort involved, the culling comes naturally.
In your dreams you see someone you don't know, but they feel like an old comrade.  Their armor shines like the sea, but it isn't armor at all.  The plates move as they breathe.
In a plane of white noise, you float blindly.  A silhouette approaches, and you see more following it as it comes near.  Some humanoid, some not.  Then you awake.
All you can remember about your dreams are gunfire, louder than anything you have ever experienced.  Such a sensory overload that it drowns out what you were shooting at.

You see a skyline on fire, awash in a thin orange haze.  You see metal cities the size of mountains.  You see countryside adorned with the skeletons of long dead war-machines.  You see an army of black, withered abominations howling and crawling over each other.  You awake with your jaw clenched and your new heart beating rapidly.

Your dreams end with the view of the skeleton of a massive superstructure, once mighty and beautiful, now picked clean to the foundation.  The wind blows through it's window-holes and the valley is filled with song.

You dream of a void of noise.  It surrounds you.  You suddenly spy a figure you cannot make out the features of.  They are massive and broad-shouldered, sitting atop a gun as large as their torso, next to what you believe is a bonfire of rebar and molten slag.  Then you wake up.

A frighteningly coherent dream stirs you awake: You cling to the roof of a ramshackle but sturdy rig, its engine screaming with effort as it tears through a great desert.  Lightning flashes at the corners of your vision to illuminate the distended bodies of fleshy blimps, as big as castles.  The rig is cornered and you dive from it onto its attackers - you need no weapon, as your body is one.

You dream you are taking part in a ritual, or ceremony of some sort.  You are led to an altar that appears more like a surgical bed, by priests adorned in green cloaks.  The cloaks do little to hide the bulk of their steel bodies underneath.

You have run out of ammo.  Gripping the searing-hot barrel of your weapon, you swing it with great force at the undead monsters closing in on you.  When your vision clears and the barrel has cooled, both the monsters and the weapon have been smashed to a pulp.  Then you wake up.

You lift up your arm, taking in the weight of its heavy plating and the power of its servos.  You lift up your other arm, and watch as it unfolds at your whim, exposing the railgun that you feel throbbing like an organ.  You then lift up your third arm, and then your fourth, and then you awake with a start.

You dream of a slender figure in the darkness, head adorned with a scarf and hands tipped with blades.  They greet you with a bow, their skeletal frame showing off flexibility that people of flesh could never accomplish.
A giant, mechanical centipede with red eyes addresses you in your dreams, but you register none of their words.  You awake after they extend an appendage to your chest.

During your dreams, an image stands out in your mind of a marble statue of some beautiful, saintly woman you think you recognize.  It depicts half of her body exposed down to the bone and organs like an anatomy bust.  The idol brings you a strange sense of comfort.
You have a nightmare about the start of the cataclysm, and your experiences in the end of the world, but…something isn't right.  You're not sure it's *your* cataclysm…but it feels like it was.

You wake from a dream that felt like it lasted for days.  A knight, just like that knight you pried the heart from, sits with you by firelight.  He lectures you on the operation and loading of several dozen weapons you have never seen in your life.  His language is alien to you, but you understand his instructions to a tee.

In perfect clarity you recall a battle, as though you were actually present.  You among dozens of your compatriots, followed by tanks and quadrupeds and vehicles armed to the teeth, sieging a citadel overrun by fused corpses reaching into the sky.  You know you may die, and are content with it - but you wake up before the fighting ends.

A dreary memory that isn't your own.  Through acrid hailstorms, you stride across the wasteland on many legs.  The sun has been blotted out from the smoke of this dying world.  Is this the fate of yours as well?

Your dreams are plagued by flickers of somewhat-related moments.  The delicate operation of a machine the size of a house.  Arrows and javelins dinking off of your metallic shell.  A quadruped stomping its foot down on a newly hatched mutant.  The same house-sized machine being gutted for parts by a legion of worker drones.
Crack.  The monstrosity's tentacle bounces off your glorious body as you swat it away.  No damage sustained…but the bastard tarnished your paint job.  In violent mercy you start up your flamer.
You wake up from a dream where you sat with a cyborg in a white void.  They were ten feet tall and adorned with etchings on their body.  They seemed to be showing you how to pray.

Your body feels cold.  Colder than normal.  When you look down you see that the enemy has torn through your iron shell, your arm lies crumpled on the floor, black ichor spills out from the exposed heart.  You fight hard not to lose consciousness, your fellow Exodii fight harder to save your life, but you know the time has come.  As your power finally shuts down and your brain dies, you sink into a void of static noise.
